clue.text: Over 100 Lilliputians sadly accepting love is mirage?

indicators.note: accepting means the jumbled letters take in another letter among them

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: sadly says the preceding letters are in a sorry, disordered state and must be rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
love is nil in tennis scores, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A traveller in Gulliver's land sees a vision of over a hundred tiny, lovelorn Lilliputians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' shuffles O, C and LILLIPUTIANS, and 'accepting' slips the O for love in among them; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is one familiar example of a trick of the eye, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stellar couples sign book in advance

indicators.note: advance says the book and in go out in front of the sign

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A cautious reader signs the book ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign book in advance' reads as booking ahead, but it means put B and IN ahead of the zodiac sign ARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call a pair of stars orbiting each other a binary star system.

clue.text: Hairy humanoid oddly ignoring my meat pie

indicators.note: oddly ignoring means the odd-placed letters are skipped and only the even ones kept

explanation.surface: A hairy creature ignores my meat pie, which is rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'my meat pie' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan abominable snowman is described as a shaggy, ape-like creature walking upright.

clue.text: Exit half-cut Finn with scarlet jumper upside down

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the name Finn is kept

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

indicators.note: upside down in a down clue means the jumper's letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: A drunken Finn in a red sweater is hanging upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (British slang for drunk) gives FI; 'jumper' is not a sweater but a kangaroo, ROO, turned to OOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire door is a fire-resistant door that also serves as an emergency exit from a building.

clue.text: Mum returns quietly after month in Split

indicators.note: after places the reversed mum and quiet letter following the month

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December

indicators.note: returns means the word for mum is turned back to front

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Mum comes home quietly after a month away in the Croatian city of Split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like the Croatian holiday city, but is the verb meaning to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for leaving suddenly or running off.

clue.text: Leader of Greece pricking Europe's uneasy conscience

indicators.note: pricking means the first letter of Greece pierces into the rearranged letters
uneasy says the letters of Europe's are unsettled and rearranged
leader of means the first letter of Greece

explanation.surface: Greece's leader troubles Europe's uneasy conscience, a picture of eurozone politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasy' rearranges EUROPES into SUPEREO, and 'pricking' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freud's model the super-ego is the part of the mind acting as moral judge, our internal sense of right and wrong.

clue.text: Summons male to move sinuously

parts.note: a writ is a legal document such as a summons
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A court order calls a man to come and wriggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist and squirm the body, as in pain, is to move in curves.

clue.text: Awfully shy friend stopping Bob vacillating

indicators.note: stopping means the scrambled letters and friend plug the middle of the coin

parts.note: a bob was British slang for a shilling, a pre-decimal coin

indicators.note: awfully says the letters of shy are badly arranged

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A painfully shy friend stops Bob from dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but a bob was British slang for a shilling, an old pre-decimal coin; 'Awfully' rearranges shy, and 'stopping' plugs the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering and wavering between choices are the same as being indecisive.

clue.text: Get ready, while attracting lots of viewers

definitions.note: the peak evening television slot, used here as an adjective

parts.note: to prime is to make ready, as with a pump or a charge
a while is a period of time

explanation.surface: A TV producer readies a show for a big audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening broadcasting slot draws the biggest television audience, and the phrase is used adjectivally for such shows.

clue.text: Pilgrimage of posh bloke ends in Andhra Pradesh

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
Mr is the title for a man

indicators.note: ends in means the last letters of the two words Andhra and Pradesh

explanation.surface: A wealthy man makes a pilgrimage that ends in an Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posh bloke' looks like one person but is two pieces, U and MR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lesser Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca, which may be made at any time of year.

clue.text: Pretend one's cool, entering declining years

parts.note: one is = I am, contracted

indicators.note: entering means the word for cool goes inside the word for declining years

parts.note: old age is a person's declining years
in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: An elderly person pretends to be cool as they grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to make believe, picturing something in the mind.

clue.text: Helping discontented barista around coffee counter

indicators.note: around means the two outer letters are turned about
discontented means the inner letters of barista are emptied out
counter means running in the opposite direction, so the coffee is read backwards

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A grumpy barista helps a customer at the coffee counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coffee counter' pictures a café, but 'counter' signals running backwards; 'discontented' empties barista and 'around' turns what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiding someone, especially in a crime, is called abetting, of which this is the noun.

clue.text: Time to abandon cabs for Central line

indicators.note: to abandon means the time letter leaves the word for cabs

parts.note: taxis are cabs

explanation.surface: Travellers give up on taxis and take the Central line on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central line is a London Underground route, but here it means a line through the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is a straight line around which a body rotates or about which it is symmetrical.

clue.text: Quite attractive guards finally stop all disruptive conduct

indicators.note: guards means the attractive word surrounds the final letters

parts.note: comely means attractive

indicators.note: finally means the last letters of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: Pretty security guards finally put an end to all unruly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives P, L, E and T, which COMELY 'guards' as COM...ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite in the sense of totally or wholly, as in quite right.

clue.text: Short, slight Arab surrounded by water

indicators.note: short means the slight word loses its last letter

parts.note: a slight is an insult
Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A short, slight Arab man is hemmed in by water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short, slight' reads as a description of a small person, but 'slight' is a noun, an insult, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally means of an island, so living on land with sea all round.

clue.text: Refuse to be buried

parts.note: reads as declining a funeral, but refuse is the noun for rubbish, which is tipped into the ground

explanation.surface: Someone declines burial after death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb (to decline); it is the noun, waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste dumped and covered with soil in a pit is the rubbish destined for burial.

clue.text: Put up with some alterations to machines

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a few changes made to the machines.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Put up' as the definition, but the verb means tolerate only as 'put up with'; 'some' alone is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something unpleasant is to be able to digest it, figuratively speaking.

clue.text: Nervous sibling consumes pot, mostly, and heroin

indicators.note: consumes means the sibling word swallows the shortened pot

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a sibling

indicators.note: mostly means the pot word loses its last letter

parts.note: a kitty is a pot or pool of money
H is drug slang for heroin, added on

explanation.surface: An anxious brother or sister smokes cannabis and takes heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' reads as cannabis next to heroin, but it is a kitty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumpy, easily startled horse or person is described as edgy and excitable.

clue.text: A magistrate disrobed after firstly cursing, out of hearing

indicators.note: after places the stripped magistrate after the first letters
firstly means take the first letter of each of the two words cursing and out
disrobed means the magistrate word is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: a justice (of the peace) is a magistrate

explanation.surface: A magistrate is stripped of the robe after swearing and storming out of a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrobed' turns JUSTICE into USTIC; 'hearing' is not a court case but the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Raving angrily? It's cause of hoarseness

indicators.note: raving means wild and frenzied, signalling the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Ranting furiously is what makes a voice go hoarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raving' rearranges ANGRILY and ITS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box is a common reason a voice goes husky or is lost.

clue.text: Thin umpire in bit of sunshine

indicators.note: in means the umpire is placed inside the ray

parts.note: a ray is a beam, a bit of sunshine
ref, short for referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: A skinny umpire stands in a patch of sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' looks like an adjective describing the umpire but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To make less dense, as air at altitude, is to dilute or thin it.

clue.text: Violet's neighbour doing somersaults round island

indicators.note: round means the tumbled letters go around the island letter
somersaults means the letters of doing are tumbled about

explanation.surface: A girl's neighbour is doing somersaults around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violet' looks like a name but is the colour; 'somersaults' rearranges DOING to INDGO, round I.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rainbow sequence this deep blue band sits next to the last colour.

clue.text: Women going into loft backwards to make deliveries

indicators.note: going into means the women letter enters the reversed loft
backwards means the word for loft is read in reverse

parts.note: to lob is to loft a ball, hitting it high

explanation.surface: Women climb backwards into a loft to deliver things.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball sent down by the bowler; 'loft' is not an attic but a high hit.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, sending the ball down to the batsman is called a delivery.

clue.text: Airily attacked Trump's revolutionary deeds on regular basis

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for trumps is reversed

parts.note: trump is British slang for breaking wind, so trump's means farts

indicators.note: on regular basis means take every other letter of deeds

explanation.surface: Political commentary on the US president's radical deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to trump is to break wind; 'revolutionary' turns FARTS into STRAF, and alternate letters of 'deeds' give ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Raking a target with gunfire from low-flying aircraft is an attack from the air.

clue.text: Communist cobblers in extremely tremulous state

indicators.note: in means the nonsense word goes inside the end letters
extremely means the two end letters of tremulous

parts.note: cobblers is British slang for nonsense, rot
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky, a US state

explanation.surface: A communist talks nonsense in a very shaky state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, not shoemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a leading Russian Marxist revolutionary.

clue.text: Using speech of Sadiq Khan, say, to oust PM

indicators.note: to oust means the prime minister is thrown out of the word

parts.note: Sadiq Khan is Mayor of London, so his office is mayoral
Theresa May was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: London's mayor uses a speech to try to unseat the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Sadiq Khan is Mayor of London; Theresa May, the PM, is removed from MAYORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written communication is by word of mouth.

clue.text: Old fellows always lacking manners? Rubbish!

parts.note: ff is the abbreviation for following, used as a doubled F for fellows

indicators.note: lacking means the manners word is missing from always

parts.note: ways are manners or customs

explanation.surface: Old men forever without manners? What nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: 'always lacking manners' leaves AL once WAYS goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal entrails are discarded parts, so the word can mean worthless refuse.

clue.text: Development of gallstone gutted Victoria, for one

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of gallstone are removed, leaving the ends

parts.note: Victoria is a London railway station

explanation.surface: A gallstone develops in Victoria, who is gutted about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth of an idea or a baby in the womb is a period of development.
